audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings may understate the post-refinancing interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $17.3 million pretax recurring-OE adjustment; computed maximum base-value effect approximately $243 million or $1.86 per share before tax
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 OE anchor retains interest expense but includes only about two months of the higher 2033-note coupon; normalizing the remaining ten months lowers sustainable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: On July 22, 2025, the Company completed an offering of $ 1,200,000,000 aggregate principal amount of its 6.000 % Senior Notes due 2033 (the “2033 Senior Notes”).
audit_findings.explanation: The new notes incur $72.0 million annual coupon interest versus $51.25 million on the replaced notes, a $20.75 million annual increase. The approximately $17.3 million missing ten-month burden, valued conservatively without a tax benefit using the base operating-PV-to-anchor multiple, reduces base value from $69.13 to about $67.27 per share. That remains above the $66.58 market price, while the buy-below conclusion remains far below market. Issuance-cost amortization is not fully quantified but is not reasonably large enough, given the filed financing amounts, to close the remaining gap.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the anchor with a full year of post-refinancing coupon interest, issuance-cost amortization and the applicable tax effect; document the resulting normalized interest expense.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments belonging partly to NCI
audit_findings.mechanism: Using parent-attributable income with consolidated D&A, capital expenditure and working-capital adjustments can misstate the parent OE numerator relative to the parent share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: Noncontrolling interests represent the equity investments of the minority owners in the Company’s joint ventures and other subsidiary entities that the Company consolidates in its financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that consolidated subsidiaries include minority interests and reports $74.4 million of FY2025 net income attributable to NCI, but it does not allocate the OE adjustments between AECOM and NCI. The sign of the error is unknown because the relevant consolidated add-backs and deductions can offset. Only about $23.7 million of recurring OE error would eliminate the $333 million base-value premium over market, so an allocation mismatch is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild FY2025 OE consistently on either a parent-attributable basis or a consolidated basis followed by an explicit NCI deduction, allocating D&A, capex, working capital and other adjustments entity by entity; rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Legacy guarantees could create an unmodeled claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: A payment under divested-business surety indemnities or the debt guarantee would reduce cash or create an equity claim not represented in forecast OE or the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company does not have sufficient information to determine the range of potential impacts; however, it is reasonably possible that the Company may incur additional costs related to these bonds.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure presently exists and the company states that additional costs are reasonably possible, but it cannot estimate the range. The broader $6.4 billion of issued surety bonds at June 2026 does not identify the amount attributable to this legacy matter, so the record cannot establish its valuation materiality or support a numerical deduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the specific bonded and guaranteed amounts, maturities, collateral, counterparty credit information, indemnity and recourse terms, probability assessment, and any included reserve; then probability-weight the net exposure in the equity bridge.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include restricted joint-venture cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $250.914 million gross bridge exposure, equal to approximately $1.92 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds total cash, including cash in consolidated joint ventures whose assets are restricted to those ventures, directly to parent equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The assets of the Company’s consolidated joint ventures are restricted for use only by the particular joint venture and are not available for the general operations of the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest balance sheet separately identifies $250.914 million of consolidated-JV cash, and the filing states that JV assets are unavailable for general corporate operations. Excluding the entire amount—a conservative maximum adjustment before recognizing AECOM's eventual economic interest—would reduce base value from $69.13 to approximately $67.21 per share. This remains above the $66.58 market price and leaves the buy-below conclusion far below market, so this finding alone does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $1,012.932 million bridge amount by legal entity and rerun the bridge using only freely distributable parent cash, adding separately any supportable parent economic interest in net JV assets.

audit_findings.title: Professional-liability reserves represent a large deferred cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $61.9 million FY2025 reserve increase; $475.3 million FY2025 reserve net of the filed $418.4 million insurance-recovery asset
audit_findings.mechanism: If the reserve increase was added as a working-capital cash source, OE reverses a current expense even though future net claim payments remain payable ahead of equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Accrued contract costs above include balances related to professional liability accruals of $ 893.7 million and $ 831.8 million as of September 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that the reserve increased from $831.8 million to $893.7 million, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether the $61.9 million increase entered the OE calculation or how FY2025 settlements and recoveries were treated. If included as a recurring working-capital source, the amount exceeds the approximately $23.7 million recurring-OE change needed to eliminate the base-value premium over market. The issue is therefore unresolved but reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the reserve expense, reserve additions, cash settlements, insurance recoveries and working-capital treatment in the FY2025 OE build; replace any reserve-growth benefit with normalized expected net cash claim payments and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unapproved claim revenue may be embedded in the anchor without a matching working-capital deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $220 million FY2025 increase, from approximately $180 million to approximately $400 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Claim revenue raises earnings before collection; omission of the associated current and non-current claim-asset increase from working capital inflates OE and therefore every DCF scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: Significant claims recorded in contract assets and other non-current assets were approximately $ 400 million and $ 180 million as of September 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $220 million increase in significant claim assets, but the record does not show how much arose from FY2025 revenue or whether all affected current and non-current assets were deducted in OE. The increase is far above the approximately $23.7 million recurring-OE error needed to erase the base-value premium. Subsequent disclosure of $620 million of claims and a $336.8 million project loss further confirms that claim recoverability is valuation-sensitive, without proving the exact FY2025 error.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each FY2025 claim's recognized revenue, incurred cost, balance-sheet location, collections and OE working-capital adjustment; probability-weight disputed claims, remove any unmatched revenue from the anchor, and rerun all scenarios.
